items.body_html: an auto action's arrival commit only CLAIMS WAITING(action_running) + ACTION_RUNNING; the runner runs post-commit via an ActionIntent (produce-not-perform), never inside the arrival commit. “Inline” is just an immediate result event, not in-commit execution

items.name_html: only an auto step re-issues the run (the LC3a/LC3b boundary)
items.body_html: both sides are guarded: post_commit_output emits an ActionIntent for action_running only when the step's trigger is auto, and ACTION_RESULT rejects a non-auto step (action_result_not_auto_action) — an operator action_running (LC3a, whose result is recorded inline in RUN_ACTION) is neither auto-issued nor completed by a kernel-event. A stuck operator action is L9 recovery. An auto step also declares no trigger-payload (no operator to supply it — auto_action_payload_unsupported at load); its inputs are the template-fixed action_spec

items.name_html: the result is a correlated kernel-event
items.body_html: ACTION_RESULT(request_id) is matched against action_running.request_id (a stale / duplicate result ⇒ action_result_mismatch), exactly like RUNTIME_CONTEXT_READY; inline vs deferred is only when it arrives

items.name_html: bounded retry is opt-in and episode-anchored
items.body_html: retry fires only for an outcome that declares retry { max_attempts, on_exhausted } — not a general negative-outcome rule — and only on an auto step (a retry outcome on an operator action is action_retry_requires_auto at load; an operator action's “retry” is the operator re-triggering a self-routed outcome). The attempt count is the ACTION_RUNNING count for the current episode_ref (transcript-reconstructable, not a hidden field); a fresh arrival opens a new episode; exhausted ⇒ route on_exhausted (escalate). Each outcome is a closed union — exactly one of { target … } or { retry … } (both ⇒ action_outcome_ambiguous_route at load; max_attempts must be a positive int; on_exhausted must resolve)

items.name_html: the recommendation rides the firing edge
items.body_html: inserting perf_test between converge and the human gate moves recommends: approve onto perf_test.pass (the edge that now enters the gate) — a clean L3 consequence (recommends is per incoming edge, runtime-selected). The L3 helpers generalize to cover it: routing_edges_with_recommends (load validation) and firing_routing_edge_into (runtime read) now span actor transitions and action outcomes, so perf_test.pass.recommends is both validated (target is a human_gate, key exists) and read at the gate — not a new mechanism
